checks.finding: Every REQ-001–REQ-007 resolves to a concrete, machine-checkable oracle: AC-001 requires a 'machine-checkable consumer_observable oracle (not a free-text description)' for REQ-001; REQ-002/AC-008 fixes idempotency as an exact diff-against-first-run check and AC-009 fixes zero-residue against a pre-install baseline; REQ-003/AC-013–AC-014 fix distinct expected-firing vs. expected-non-firing cell states rather than a single pass/fail; REQ-004/AC-018–AC-020 fix per-cell source bytes/resolved path/copied bytes/stdout/residue oracles; REQ-005/AC-022–AC-023 fix a distinct not-installed/synced/drifted state set with mode-dependent exit semantics; REQ-006/AC-025–AC-026 fix an exhaustive classification table and a fully-enumerated record schema. No in-scope REQ is left as unmeasurable intent.

Every stated goal traces to at least one AC in acceptance-tests.md's Requirement column: REQ-001→AC-001–AC-006, REQ-002→AC-007–AC-011, REQ-003→AC-012–AC-017 and AC-028, REQ-004→AC-018–AC-021, REQ-005→AC-022–AC-024, REQ-006→AC-025–AC-027, REQ-007→AC-029–AC-030 (requirements.md REQ-007 text names this same mapping explicitly, including the AC-029/AC-030 exception, and acceptance-tests.md's table matches it row-for-row).

Acceptance criteria consistently specify externally observable artifacts rather than intent: AC-001 fixes exact artifact path/initial bytes/mutation/final bytes/hash; AC-008 fixes idempotency as 'a registered/copied state identical to the first run — no duplicate marketplace entries, no duplicate config.toml blocks'; AC-013/AC-014 fix named, distinguishable cell states (e.g. `CAPABILITY_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`) rather than a generic pass/fail; AC-023 fixes a three-way distinct state (not-installed / synced / drifted) with mode-dependent exit codes. No AC in the reviewed set relies on unmeasurable adjectives alone.

requirements.md's Non-goals section explicitly excludes: re-implementing any Epic A1–A7's own per-Epic 3-environment work (INV-001); building/registering any new CI job or workflow file; specifying `--target FilesOnly` behavior (AC-011 additionally asserts this is 'recorded out-of-scope... never silently treated as a fifth matrix cell'); re-specifying Epic A1's canonicalizer or Epic A5's caller-contract fixture; and any change to `plugins/**`, `scripts/**`, `.github/**`, `tests/**`, `contracts/**`, or `docs/**` in this task. AC-029 additionally makes this boundary self-checkable ('no AC above names a new .sh/.ps1 pair... for another Epic's own surface').

Material constraints are explicit: the Security Boundaries table fixes two named trust boundaries (B1 live-host session authenticity/attribution, B2 read-only drift comparison with 'no auto-remediation, no silent re-install') with PII/data-classification and regulatory columns populated ('none identified'); Roles and Permissions fixes a two-party attestation requirement (operator + independent reviewer, distinct identities) before a live-host record is treated as authoritative (AC-026/AC-027); AC-026 fixes an exhaustive field list for the manual-session record including nonce ledger, key IDs, and signature verification, closing the approval-boundary gap this epic's safety-critical claim (ADR-0019 delegation) would otherwise leave open.

The Risks section names three high-risk claims, each tied to a concrete validation surface already fixed elsewhere in the package: the Critical risk (REQ-003 live-host proof may remain permanently manual-required if no CLI's headless mode supports the canary pattern) is explicitly routed to REQ-006's classification table (AC-025) as 'an accepted, explicitly-classified outcome... rather than a defect'; the High risk (extending `cli-hook-enforcement.ps1` could entangle synthetic regression with live-host proof status) is routed to AC-017's structural-independence assertion; the Medium risk (deliberate 4-file Phase-1 scope) is routed to the named `check-sdd-structure.sh` expected-missing-file list and Epic A7's own established precedent (INV-018). No high-risk claim is left without a named downstream check or artifact.
